newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal 10-yr bond yield hits low at 7.96 pct.
newsitem.headline: Portugal 10-yr bond yield hits low at 7.96 pct.

text.p: The yield on Portuguese 10-year bonds dropped below eight percent for the first time to a record low of 7.96 percent, dealers said.

"Although the players are mainly domestic and liquidity is thin, the December 1996 future has risen to close to 100 points and 10-year yields dropped to a record low below eight percent," a fixed rate director said.
The price of the December 1996 future rose 0.49 percent to 99.98 points, while its Spanish equivalent rose 0.59 percent to 106.43 points.
February 2006 Portuguese bonds traded with a yield of 7.96 percent to give a yield spread of four basis points (bp) above January 2006 Bonos and 190 bp above April 2006 Bunds.

"The surge in Portuguese bonds is in line with Spain and is due to optimism that our economy will qualify to join a single European currency," an operator said. "The hope is that southern European countries will present rigorous 1997 budgets and that Portugal is not the exception."

The fixed rate director said "In futures, there is some resistance to a break through 100 points, with selling appearing close to these levels; but if Spain rises further, the market will surpass this level."
